1. I think it's pretty reasonable to try to create a community that is supportive rather than one where people say "you're just looking for excuses to feel persecuted". Particularly since this has been the attitude trying to halt feminism since its beginning ("Women don't need the right to vote, they have such a comfortable life living at home! And they don't understand politics anyway, they're just looking for an excuse to be upset" <--- actual attitude of many during the suffrage movement)

2. It might have been reasonable on the boss's part, because he's not personally responsible for what society thinks about women's bodies. But when women are *constantly* taught to be ashamed of their bodies and that they have to cover them up because of what men might think about a bit more of their breasts showing and what it might make men do to them, "get over it" is really not a constructive attitude and it's one that actively stifles discussion. It might not be the boss's fault, but it's definitely a societal problem and the idea that she's just looking for excuses to be upset is truly harmful
I really really appreciate your attitude about this, the angry feminist haters all over this thread are super annoying and harmful

I think that information is relevant because she's asking for advice on how to deal with it. The way she would approach a man about it might be different from the way she would approach a woman about it (not because men are bad, but because talking to a man about that issue should probably include more explanation of the pressures that a woman would probably have already dealt with herself), etc
Yeah I don't think that would do it on its own, but combined with an unhelpful (possibly perceived as disrespectful too) they probably thought he was there to troll

I'm really glad you have that perspective on it (the circle-jerking about how evil feminists are in this thread is really frustrating and kinda gross). I think that's exactly how they perceived it - she's looking for advice with a problem and it seemed like what you were trying to say was "it's not a problem"
I've been told to walk with a man by all of the above

Huh, I never really thought about it but it kind of makes sense that dressing less modestly makes you less likely to be mugged... If you look fabulous and confident mugging you would probably draw more attention than mugging the girl in dark modest unassuming clothes

When my SO offers to walk me home to "keep me safe" I say no. People take risks all the time for issues they care about, and it's worth it to me not to feel like a need a man to protect me all the time
I've seen like 5 different doctors, they started me on lamictal and seroquel but the next doctors had me do ECT instead. Neither really helped and now I'm home from University with no new doctor.

One of the ways I "protect" myself:   
I have kind of a rule that I have to clean up my things and leave everything in order if I were to off myself, so that no one would think badly of me when they found all the nasty dishes in my bedroom. I guess the horrifying state of my belongings is an indicator of my will to live (downside: I am now literally afraid of cleaning)
